 Cavaliers reportedly reach deal with DirecTV amid frustration over DAZN accessibility
 Entering the season, the Cavs were one of five NBA teams to sign an exclusive local broadcast deal with DAZN. 
 Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images 
 By Drew Lerner on 10/25/2026 10/25/2026 
 Less AI and more AA in your search results.
 The Cleveland Cavaliers were one of five NBA teams that entered this season with an exclusive deal with DAZN, the London-based streaming service making a push into the U.S. market through a series of local NBA broadcast deals. But it seems like the Cavs might be making an effort to make their local games a bit more accessible.
 According to a report by Danny Cunningham, a Cavaliers reporter who appears on 92.3 The Fan in Cleveland as well as the  Locked on Cavs podcast, the Cavs and DAZN have reached an agreement with DirecTV that will see the team’s games become available on DirecTV platforms. A formal announcement is expected this week, Cunningham writes, but it appears the deal kicked in for the Cavaliers’ home opener against the Brooklyn Nets on Saturday.
 Source: The #Cavs and DAZN reached an agreement with DirecTV to air games this season, beginning tonight with the team’s home opener against the Brooklyn Nets. The game will be available to DirecTV customers on channel 660.
 Formal announcement is expected next week.
 — Danny Cunningham (@RealDCunningham) October 24, 2026 
 Prior to Saturday, the only way for in-market fans to access Cavs broadcasts was to purchase a subscription with DAZN, which runs about $120 for the season. When the DAZN deal was first reported in September, Sports Business Journal reported the arrangement would pay the Cavs a rights fee of around $20 million annually. The exclusivity of the deal allowed the Cavs to command a substantially higher fee than teams that opted to join DAZN on a streaming-only basis while striking other deals with linear television providers. It’s unclear if the financial terms of the team’s original deal will be modified to reflect DAZN’s lack of exclusivity.
 Prior to the season, Awful Announcing ranked the Cavaliers as the least-accessible NBA team in the league . The Cavs were one of five teams without a linear television option, other than a simulcast deal to air 15 games over the air (which has become common throughout the league). But due to the number of Cavs games scheduled for national windows, only 59 games would be available via DAZN this season. That means Cavs fans would need both DAZN and a variety of other streamers to watch substantial portions of their team’s season.
 Now, it seems like the team is reversing course, at least to an extent. Whether the DirecTV deal is a precursor to other linear television deals is unclear. It’s also unclear if the Cavaliers will offer refunds to fans that purchased a DAZN subscription only to later find out it was not necessary because they are already DirecTV subscribers.
 Regardless, the Cavs are at least taking steps to make their games a bit easier to watch for fans, even if it took some light public shaming to happen.
